slides.title: Actions and Activities
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 5: Actions and Activities. You will learn thirteen action words, including build, discuss, protect and celebrate. You will talk about what you did using the past simple, explain reasons and results with because and so, order events with First, Next, Then and Finally, ask Wh- questions, and share opinions politely. The unit story, “The Wall Behind the Garden”, follows Amal, Leo and their class as they build a reading wall together. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name and use many action words, such as build, listen, protect and celebrate.
Talk about things you did, using the past simple (built, listened, celebrated).
Explain why something happened, using because and so.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name and use many action words, such as build, listen, protect and celebrate. You will also talk about things you did, using the past simple (built, listened, celebrated). You will also explain why something happened, using because and so. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: discuss, listen, offer, build, complete, remove. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes A Busy Saturday and Helping Hands. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: The Past Simple Tense
bullets: We use the past simple to talk about actions that already happened and are finished. It helps us tell stories and share the things we did. In this unit's...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is The Past Simple Tense. We use the past simple to talk about actions that already happened and are finished. It helps us tell stories and share the things we did. In this unit's story the children built a wall, so we say built, not build. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Tell What You Did. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
